analysis.title: The Point for North America, Tuesday, 03 November 2026
key_insights: Apple reported better than expected Sept-quarter results. The December-quarter outlook was mixed against the Street: higher product revenue, offset by lower Services growth and lower gross margin. Management blamed incremental fx headwinds and third-party licensing for the Services slowdown. Gross margin pressure came from memory costs, higher inference costs from Siri AI and increased hardware deferral costs. Citi keeps Buy and a $365 target on 33x P/E applied to revised FY28 EPS.

Citi expects the FASB to finalize an update in 1Q27 that lets banks apply fair value or cash flow hedge accounting to their Held-to-Maturity securities portfolios. Citi calls this a structural positive for the sector because it removes accounting-driven earnings volatility and makes net interest margins reflect hedging economics. BAC, PNC and WFC are named as the main beneficiaries, and ROE is the key metric to watch.

Citi opened a positive 30-day catalyst watch on Petrobras (PBR ADR and PETR4). The case rests on high oil and gas production, elevated crack spreads (mainly diesel) and oil prices from supply disruptions tied to the Russia-Ukraine and Middle East conflicts. The new strategic plan is due November 24th. The stock has trended lower since the surprise in the Brazilian presidential election.

Palantir's Q3 revenue growth accelerated both y/y and q/q, led by U.S. Commercial and Government. Q4 guidance implies growth of +15% to +16% q/q, the strongest guidance since the IPO. Sovereign AI deals carried shorter contract durations, which produced weaker TCV and other bookings metrics. Citi reads the revenue acceleration and the raised Q4 outlook as evidence of underlying ACV strength. It lifts 2026-2027 revenue, EPS and FCF estimates by 4-7% and raises the target to $265 from $250.

Vertex's 3Q26 revenue was $3.44B (+12% y/y) with non-GAAP EPS of $4.76, and FY26 revenue guidance was raised to a $13.2B midpoint. Alyftrek grew +186% y/y, Casgevy grew +30% q/q and Crinetics' Palsonify added its first $10M. Investor focus stays on the late-stage pipeline, especially povetacicept in IgAN (11/30 PDUFA). Citi maintains Buy with a $585 target.

SBA Communications reported domestic leasing slightly below Citi and consensus expectations. Citi now forecasts AFFOPS near flat in 2027, with growth more likely to start in 2028. Contributing factors are consolidation churn, Brazil FX headwinds and potentially higher refinancing costs. The target is cut to $225 on estimate changes and a higher cost of capital. Citi's revised forecasts imply average downside to consensus for CY2027E-CY2029E of about 3% on EBITDA and about 2% on AFFOPS.

Advanced Energy delivered a beat-and-raise quarter. Management now expects 2027 revenue growth of 30% y/y versus 20%+ before, driven by data center and semis, despite some supply constraints. Citi lifts CY26/CY27 EPS estimates by 9%/10%, introduces CY28 EPS of $24.33, and trims the target to $450 (from $460) on 24x CY27 EPS to reflect lower market multiples. Rating stays Buy.

Krystal Biotech had a mixed quarter. Positives were EU Vyjuvek launch momentum, apparently favorable German pricing and an unexpected $400M buyback with $1.2B on the balance sheet. Negatives were three data readouts (NK, B-VEC, CF) pushed into 2027 and non-GAAP OpEx guidance lowered to $155-165M from $175-195M. Citi expects R&D to ramp about 30% in 2027. Target goes to $412 from $416, Buy, High risk.

Eastman Chemical takeaways: a $375mm DOE grant could fund up to 50% of qualifying project capital including a Kingsport methanolysis debottleneck, which would lower projected capex. Management reiterated 3% FY26 volume growth in AM and expects volumes up across AM, A&FP and Fibers in 2027. Acetate tow pricing is expected to fall another mid-single-digit percent in 2027. Methanolysis revenue could add up to about $100mm in 2026 and another about $100mm in 2027.

Estee Lauder's F1Q27 results beat across the P&L, with organic sales growth in three of four categories (fragrance +20%) and in every region. Innovation was 29% of sales. FY27 guidance was raised for OSG, operating margin and EPS. The stock closed down on high expectations into the print. Citi reiterates Buy and raises the target to $121.

Citi's 3Q26 cloud compare shows top-4 cloud industry growth accelerating about 9 points to +58.6% y/y. Azure grew +48% y/y cc, AWS +39.3%, Google Cloud +103% and OCI about +120% cc. Google Cloud gained about 200bps of share to 26% and OCI about 65bps to about 6.3%, while AWS lost 210bps q/q but remains the leader at 39% and Azure slipped about 50bps to about 28%. Combined capex rose about $28B q/q to about $146B.

Citi's oil and gas equipment note argues a wave of behind-the-meter power contracts may be starting. SEI announced its largest contract, a 15-year 900MW supply deal. Williams and Atlas report this evening, and Citi expects two more projects from Williams with longer tenures. LBRT forecasts its first power contract by year-end. Sentiment on the theme has soured, and Citi sees the pullback as an opportunity to re-engage.
Citi expects electric utility capex to keep accelerating with a growing generation weighting. EEI conference meetings and earnings over the next two weeks should reinforce both trends.

At TCT, Edwards published PROGRESS data validating TAVR for moderate aortic stenosis, plus strong CLASP II TR data for its PASCAL tricuspid repair device. An existing NCD leaves room for CMS to cover moderate AS, which Citi says supports the higher end of Edwards' mid-to-high-single-digit TAVR growth forecast for 2027+. Boston Scientific's SIMPLAAFY RCT results should benefit Watchman utilization. Citi rates EW Buy and BSX Neutral.

Citi's retail desk notes last week's earnings: BOOT had a short squeeze rally on October same-store sales above expectations, ORLY same-store sales beat but EPS flow-through disappointed, and FND lowered guidance on higher mortgage rates. A CHWY CFO meeting suggested the company can outgrow a muted pet market. AAP reports Thursday.

Across TSCO, BOOT, ORLY and FND calendar 3Q reports, most names beat on sales and EPS, with a slight EPS miss at BOOT. Guidance was mixed: only ORLY raised full-year guidance, TSCO held, and BOOT and FND lowered. BOOT and TSCO are the best performers since earnings and FND the worst.

Citi forecasts October nonfarm payrolls of +65k with unemployment unchanged at 4.2%. It expects softer job growth in coming months partly because of a smaller labor force. Slowing average hourly earnings would reaffirm Chair Warsh's claim that the economy is not overheated and could limit a hawkish market reaction to an upside employment surprise.

ISM manufacturing rose to 55.5 in October, staying expansionary all year. Citi will watch ISM new orders for signs of slowing, with headwinds including weaker AI-related sentiment, higher rates and tighter financial conditions, and fading tax incentives into 2027.

Behind-the-meter power contract announcements may be starting, and Citi sees the recent pullback as a re-entry opportunity.
Capex plans are accelerating with a larger generation weighting, expected to continue through earnings and EEI meetings.

earnings_insights: AAPL reported Sept-quarter (FQ4'26) results better than expected. The December-quarter outlook was mixed against Street expectations, with higher product revenue offset by lower Services growth and lower gross margin. No figures are given in this summary.

PLTR reported Q3 2026 with revenue growth accelerating y/y and q/q. Q4 guidance implies revenue growth of 88% y/y versus 75% prior guidance, or +16% q/q (guided +15% q/q). Bookings and TCV were weaker because Sovereign AI deals had shorter durations.

VRTX 3Q26 reported revenue of $3.44B (+12% y/y) and non-GAAP EPS of $4.76. FY26 revenue guidance was raised to a $13.2B midpoint. Alyftrek +186% y/y, Casgevy +30% q/q, Palsonify first contribution $10M.
SBAC 3Q26 domestic leasing was slightly below Citi and consensus expectations. Citi now forecasts 2027 AFFOPS near flat.
AEIS reported a beat-and-raise quarter. Management guided 2027 revenue growth to 30% y/y versus 20%+ prior. Citi raises CY26/CY27 EPS estimates by 9%/10% and introduces a CY28 EPS estimate of $24.33.
KRYS reported a quarter with non-GAAP OpEx guidance lowered to $155-165M from $175-195M, a $400M buyback and $1.2B on the balance sheet. NK, B-VEC and CF data were pushed into 2027.
EMN reiterated 3% FY26 volume growth in AM, implying mid-to-high-single-digit growth in 4Q. It expects up to about $100mm of methanolysis revenue in 2026 and about $100mm more growth in 2027.

EL reported F1Q27 results that beat expectations across the P&L. It raised FY27 guidance to OSG of 4.0%-5.5%, operating margin of 12.9%-13.7% and EPS of $3.20-$3.45. Innovation was 29% of sales versus an expected 25% for FY27.
Cloud 3Q26 reported growth: Azure +48% y/y cc, AWS +39.3% y/y, Google Cloud +103% y/y, OCI about +120% y/y cc. Combined capex was about $146B, up about $28B q/q.

Retail calendar 3Q: ORLY, TSCO, BOOT and FND mostly beat on sales and EPS (slight EPS miss at BOOT). Only ORLY raised full-year guidance, TSCO held, and BOOT and FND lowered. BOOT October same-store sales were above market expectations.
Williams and Atlas report earnings this evening. AAP reports Thursday.
